what: versus.py takes a float (`factor`) and a list of nested dataclasses with an optional field; ran.py's typed-input parser reads no float, so versus.py carries a second copy of `parsed`/`fitted` that does.
cost: two parsers of one rule (scripts-take-typed-input) that can drift
cause: ran.py's `fitted` grew one type at a time for its own callers instead of covering JSON's types once
class: a shared helper that covers only what its first callers needed, copied by the next caller
prevention: one typed-input parser for harness scripts that covers every JSON type (number as float, nested and optional dataclasses), and scripts import it
workaround: versus.py's own parser, same refusals as ran.py's
fix: Wanted (not made, ran.py is outside track 8): ran.fitted reads `float` (an int or float JSON number) and versus.py imports ran.parsed and deletes its copy.
